newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major says BSE crisis cost about 3.3 bln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major says BSE crisis cost about 3.3 bln stg.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday the cost of the mad cow disease crisis and the European export ban on British beef is around 3.3 billion sterling.

Asked by Labour leader Tony Blair if he could confirm that the cost was now 3.3 billion pounds, Blair told parliament: "The cost is of that order, that is correct." But Major added that much of this cost was due to health scares begun by Labour.
"Throughout this whole affair the government has been entirely open with the British nation and the Labour party repeatedly has tried to stoke up health fears at home and abroad," Major said.
Major accused Blair of undermining Britain's position in Europe just as Britain was preparing to present proposals to the European Union designed to end the EU's export ban.
Labour has called a debate on Monday over the government's handling of the mad cow crisis.

With the Conservatives currently tied with all the opposition parties combined, Labour is trying to engineer a government defeat in the debate, which is specifically on Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg's handling of the crisis.
If Labour wins, this would force Hogg to resign and increase pressure on Major to call an immediate general election.
Defeat could also trigger a no-confidence vote in Major's government, although Labour has said it is not yet speculating about such a vote. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7768
